presets.label: Recommended (1080p)
presets.help: True 1920x1080, single-tile scene, MSAA off, the 60 fps profile with late-frame release and the Performance scene-detail preset. On a Radeon 880M in Performance mode: 60 fps most of the time (parked scene 60.0 fps, 99th percentile 17.1 ms); in the heaviest streets the game may hold 30 fps for 6-18 s (see Max hold at 30 fps). Pick Balanced or Performance if your GPU is slower.

presets.label: 16:10 panel 60 (1920x1200)
presets.help: A 1920x1200 (16:10) render at the 60 fps profile with the Performance scene-detail preset: fills a 16:10 panel with no black bars. On a Radeon 880M in Performance mode it behaves like 1080p: 60 fps most of the time (parked scene 60.0 fps, 99th percentile 17.2 ms), with a 6-18 s hold at 30 fps in the heaviest streets.

presets.label: Balanced (900p 60)
presets.help: 1600x900 at the 60 fps profile, no upscaler, scaled to the screen by the presenter: a lighter load than 1080p.

presets.label: Performance (720p 60)
presets.help: The shipped 1280x720 at the 60 fps profile with MSAA off and the Performance scene-detail preset: the lightest 60 fps setup (60.00 fps, 99th percentile 17.4 ms on a Radeon 880M in Performance mode).

presets.label: FSR 4 (1080p from 540p, experimental)
presets.help: A 1920x1080 picture with the 3D scene drawn at 960x540 and upscaled by AMD FSR 4 (the 1080p-fsr4p profile: 2x, sharpness 0.2). Needs AMD's signed runtime DLLs next to mcla.exe and a Radeon RDNA 2 or newer / 800M series GPU; otherwise it runs FSR 3.1.6. Experimental: 37 fps measured on a Radeon 880M, slower than native 1080p.

presets.label: 16:10 panel, fastest (1280x800, display mode switch)
presets.help: A 1280x800 (16:10) render at the 60 fps profile for a 16:10 laptop panel. Fullscreen switches the display to the game's mode (the highest multiple of 60 Hz, 120 preferred) so the panel's scaler fills the screen with no black bars; falls back to desktop scaling if the display has no such mode.

presets.label: Native panel 3200x2000 (about 25 fps)
presets.help: A true 3200x2000 picture for the 3200x2000 laptop panel: the game renders 1600x1000 and draws every render target at 2x2, about 4x the GPU load (23-26 fps measured on a Radeon 880M, parked scene). The 60 fps profile runs unlocked below 60 with a variable simulation step, so the game's speed stays right (world/real 1.000). Sun-shadow map 384 (768 host texels, close to the shipped 640). Fullscreen uses the desktop size (borderless); do not switch the display mode, it would go to 1600x1000.

presets.label: Shipped (console 30)
presets.help: The console's own look and timing: 1280x720, 2x MSAA, locked 30 fps.

settings.label: Resolution
settings.help: The size the game renders and presents at. 16:10 sizes use a wider vertical camera (Vert+) and keep the HUD in a 16:9 band. Anything above 720p needs the 4096-tile EDRAM the game's profile already sets.

options.label: 1280x720 (shipped, 16:9)
options.help: The console's own size. With MSAA off it is the cheapest setting.

options.label: 1280x800 (16:10)
options.help: Matches a 16:10 laptop panel. Vert+ camera, HUD in a 16:9 band.

options.label: 1440x900 (16:10)
options.help: 16:10 at 900 rows. Vert+ camera, HUD in a 16:9 band.

options.label: 1600x900 (16:9)
options.help: A step below 1080p: a lighter load than 1920x1080, scaled to the screen by the presenter.

options.label: 1600x1000 (16:10)
options.help: 16:10 at 1000 rows. Vert+ camera, HUD in a 16:9 band.

options.label: 1920x1080 (16:9)
options.help: True 1920x1080 render, MSAA off. On a Radeon 880M in Performance mode with the Performance scene-detail preset: 60 fps most of the time, with occasional holds at 30 fps in the heaviest streets.

options.label: 1920x1200 (16:10)
options.help: 16:10 at 1200 rows. Vert+ camera, HUD in a 16:9 band. Fills a 16:10 panel with no black bars; on a Radeon 880M it measured the same as 1920x1080 (60 fps most of the time, occasional holds at 30 fps).

options.label: 3200x2000 (16:10, native laptop panel)
options.help: The game renders 1600x1000 and every render target is drawn at 2x2, so the picture is a true 3200x2000 (Vert+ camera, HUD in a 16:9 band); about 4x the GPU load of 1600x1000, measured 23-26 fps on a Radeon 880M (parked scene). Use Fullscreen mode "Desktop size (borderless)": with "Switch the display to the game's mode" the display would go to 1600x1000.

settings.label: Fullscreen
settings.help: Start in a borderless fullscreen window. Off gives a normal window (see Window width / height).

settings.label: Fullscreen mode
settings.help: How fullscreen is done: scale the picture on the desktop, switch the display to the game's video mode, or switch it to a fixed mode.

options.label: Desktop size (borderless)
options.help: Borderless window at the desktop's size; the game scales (and letterboxes) the picture itself. Safe everywhere.

options.label: Switch the display to the game's mode
options.help: Changes the display mode to the game's video mode (e.g. 1280x800 or 1920x1080) at the highest refresh rate that is a multiple of 60 Hz (120 preferred), so the monitor's own scaler fills the panel. Falls back to the desktop size (see the log) if the display has no such mode. Do not use it with the 3200x2000 resolution: the display would go to the game's 1600x1000.

options.label: 1280x800 @ 120 Hz (display mode)
options.help: Switches the display to exactly 1280x800 at 120 Hz (a 16:10 laptop panel mode); the panel's scaler fills the screen. Falls back to the desktop size if the display has no such mode.

options.label: 1600x1000 @ 120 Hz (display mode)
options.help: Switches the display to exactly 1600x1000 at 120 Hz (16:10); the panel's scaler fills the screen. Falls back to the desktop size if the display has no such mode.

options.label: 1920x1200 @ 120 Hz (display mode)
options.help: Switches the display to exactly 1920x1200 at 120 Hz (16:10); the panel's scaler fills the screen. Falls back to the desktop size if the display has no such mode.

settings.label: Window width
settings.help: Width of the game window in pixels when not fullscreen. 0 = follow the resolution above.

settings.label: Window height
settings.help: Height of the game window in pixels when not fullscreen. 0 = follow the resolution above.

settings.label: Monitor
settings.help: Which display the game opens on: 0 = default display; N = the Nth display in SDL's list.

settings.label: Keep aspect ratio (letterbox)
settings.help: On: a picture whose aspect differs from the window is shown with black bars. Off: it is stretched to fill the window (distorted).

settings.label: 16:10 camera
settings.help: Camera on a back buffer taller than 16:9 (the 16:10 sizes: 1280x800, 1440x900, 1600x1000, 1920x1200 and 3200x2000). Has no effect at 16:9 sizes.

options.label: Vert+ (wider vertical view)
options.help: The vertical angle is widened so the horizontal view stays the 16:9 one. Recommended.

options.label: Hor- (the game's own)
options.help: The vertical angle stays; the sides of the view are cut.

settings.label: Allow tearing / variable refresh rate
settings.help: Direct3D 12 presents with tearing allowed, so G-Sync / FreeSync work and a late frame is not held to the next refresh. Turn off if you see tearing you dislike.

settings.label: HDR output (experimental)
settings.help: HDR10 (BT.2020 PQ). Auto: HDR when Windows HDR (Settings > Display > Use HDR) is on for the window's display. The game's look up to 60% of its white, real highlights above it up to the display's peak; HUD and menus at Windows' SDR content brightness. Measured cost: about 0.1-0.3 ms GPU per frame at 1080p on a Radeon 880M. Not yet judged by eye on an HDR screen.

options.label: Off
options.help: Standard dynamic range.

options.label: Auto
options.help: HDR when the display is in HDR mode.

options.label: On
options.help: Always HDR10, even on an SDR desktop (Windows converts it back; use Auto).

settings.label: HDR peak brightness (nits)
settings.help: The brightest the highlights go. 0 = what Windows reports for the display (run the Windows HDR Calibration app for a measured value). Lower it if highlights clip.

settings.label: HDR paper white (nits)
settings.help: Where the game's white lands in HDR. 0 = Windows' SDR content brightness slider (the desktop's white).

settings.label: HDR HUD and menu brightness (nits)
settings.help: Brightness of the HUD, menus and movies in HDR. 0 = paper white.

settings.label: HDR highlights
settings.help: How far bright things go above the game's white: 1 normal, 1.5 bright, 2 brighter (default), 3 brightest.

settings.label: HDR shadow curve
settings.help: How the game's colours are decoded in HDR. 2.2 gamma (default) keeps the deep blacks of the TVs the game was made for (right for OLED); sRGB matches how Windows shows SDR apps on an HDR desktop (lighter shadows).

settings.label: Disable MSAA (no anti-aliasing)
settings.help: Creates the renderer without the game's 2x MSAA: one 1x scene instead of two 2x tiles, a clearly cheaper frame with slightly more jagged edges. Needed for the FSR upscaler; the 1080p and 900p sizes switch it on by themselves. Takes effect at start.

settings.label: Upscaler (AMD FSR)
settings.help: AMD FSR temporal upscaling: the 3D scene is drawn smaller and upscaled to the output size, with temporal anti-aliasing. HUD and post-processing stay at full size. Needs: MSAA disabled, Single-tile scene on, Direct3D 12. On a Radeon 880M it measured slower than native 1080p (FSR 3: 49 fps, FSR 4: 37 fps against 60), so it only pays off where shading dominates.

options.label: Off (native resolution)
options.help: The scene is drawn at the output size, no temporal pass.

options.label: AMD FSR (temporal upscaler)
options.help: Draws the scene at output size divided by the quality ratio and upscales it with the FSR version chosen below.

settings.label: FSR version
settings.help: Which FSR runs. FSR 4 (the machine-learning upscaler) needs AMD's signed runtime DLLs next to mcla.exe and a supported Radeon; without the DLLs the FSR 3.1 built into the game runs whatever this says.

options.label: FSR 3.1
options.help: AMD FSR 3.1 (the temporal upscaler built into the game; FSR 3.1.6 with AMD's runtime). 49 fps measured on a Radeon 880M.

options.label: FSR 4 (ML)
options.help: AMD's machine-learning upscaler (experimental here; 37 fps measured on a Radeon 880M); the game falls back to FSR 3.1.6 where the GPU or the runtime does not offer it.

options.label: Auto (FSR 4 if available, else FSR 3.1)
options.help: FSR 4.1 on RDNA 2 and newer and the Radeon 800M series when AMD's signed runtime is next to mcla.exe, else FSR 3.1.

settings.label: FSR quality
settings.help: How much smaller the scene is drawn than the output (the ratio). Higher = faster and softer. At 1920x1080: Quality 1280x720, Balanced 1129x635, Performance 960x540.

options.label: Native AA (1.0x)
options.help: No upscaling: FSR only anti-aliases at the output size.

options.label: Ultra Quality (1.33x)
options.help: Scene at three quarters of the output size.

options.label: Quality (1.5x)
options.help: Scene at two thirds of the output size (1280x720 for 1080p).

options.label: Balanced (1.7x)
options.help: A little less than two thirds of the output size.

options.label: Performance (2x)
options.help: Scene at half the output size (960x540 for 1080p). The FSR 4 preset uses it.

options.label: Ultra Performance (3x)
options.help: Scene at a third of the output size. Visibly soft.

settings.label: FSR sharpness
settings.help: Sharpening (RCAS) applied after FSR, 0 = off to 1 = strongest. 0.3 suits FSR 3.1; 0.2 is the SDK default and what the FSR 4 preset uses.

settings.label: Output scaling filter
settings.help: How the finished picture is scaled to the window when the sizes differ. FSR 1 is a spatial upscaler (EASU + RCAS) and costs some GPU time; CAS only sharpens.

options.label: Bilinear (default)
options.help: The plain GPU filter. No extra cost.

options.label: CAS (sharpen)
options.help: AMD contrast-adaptive sharpening on top of the plain filter.

options.label: FSR 1 (spatial upscale)
options.help: AMD FSR 1 on the finished picture, HUD included. Best with a render size below the window size.

settings.label: Post-process anti-aliasing (FXAA)
settings.help: FXAA over the finished frame (HUD included), about 0.3 ms GPU at 1080p on a Radeon 880M. Smooths the stair-stepped edges the game has without MSAA. Changes while playing (no restart); skipped while HDR output is active.

options.label: Off
options.help: No post-process anti-aliasing.

options.label: FXAA
options.help: Standard FXAA (recommended when there is GPU headroom).

options.label: FXAA (extreme)
options.help: Stronger edge search; slightly softer picture, about the same cost.

settings.label: Anisotropic filtering
settings.help: Forces anisotropic filtering on textures: sharper at oblique angles (road surfaces), at a small GPU cost.

options.label: Game default
options.help: No override: each texture is filtered as the game asks.

options.label: Off
options.help: Trilinear filtering only.

options.label: 2x
options.help: Two-times anisotropic filtering.

options.label: 4x
options.help: Four-times anisotropic filtering (the SDK's default).

options.label: 8x
options.help: Eight-times anisotropic filtering.

options.label: 16x
options.help: Sixteen-times anisotropic filtering (the profile's default; the cost is small).

settings.label: Texture sharpness (mip bias)
settings.help: Shifts texture mip selection toward sharper levels: 0 = as the game asks; -0.5 = sharper distant textures. Without anti-aliasing a negative bias adds shimmer, so pair it with FXAA. Practically free on the GPU. Changes while playing.

settings.label: Scene detail preset
settings.help: A bundle of the scene-detail knobs below, applied at start: Performance for weak GPUs, Quality and Ultra for GPUs with headroom (they add FXAA). A knob you change below wins over the preset's value for it.

options.label: Full (as shipped)
options.help: No change to the game's own detail levels.

options.label: Quality
options.help: The game's full detail (car reflections and all shadow cascades every frame, shipped shadow and detail distances, 640 shadow map) plus FXAA. About 1.5 ms more GPU time than Performance at 1080p on a Radeon 880M: only with headroom.

options.label: Ultra (beyond console)
options.help: Quality with the shadow, city and vehicle detail distances at 1.5x the console's: less pop-in in the distance, about 1 ms more GPU time while driving.

options.label: Performance
options.help: Car reflections and the second-farthest shadow cascade updated every 2nd frame (30 Hz, the console's own rate), shadow distance 0.6, vehicle LOD 0.7, city LOD 0.67, sun-shadow map 512: a near-identical picture, about 5 points less GPU load at 1080p on a Radeon 880M.

options.label: Performance+
options.help: Performance plus no far shadow cascade and no tree impostors.

options.label: Lowest
options.help: Performance plus no sun shadows (the game's own night path): the largest saving, at the price of every sun shadow.

settings.label: Detail tier (run-time)
settings.help: One switch for the live scene-detail knobs, used by the frame-rate governor; it overrides the knobs above while set. Changes while playing.

options.label: Off (use the knobs)
options.help: No tier: the knobs above decide.

options.label: 0: emergency (no sun shadows)
options.help: Lowest tier: no sun shadows.

options.label: 1: Performance
options.help: The Performance detail level.

options.label: 2: Performance + FXAA
options.help: Performance plus FXAA.

options.label: 3: shipped distances + FXAA
options.help: The game's shipped shadow and detail distances plus FXAA.

options.label: 4: Quality (live part)
options.help: The live part of the Quality preset.

options.label: 5: Ultra distances
options.help: Quality with the shadow, city and vehicle detail distances at 1.5x the console's.

settings.label: Sun-shadow map size
settings.help: Edge of the sun-shadow map in texels. Smaller is cheaper and softer. Read when a world loads (restart or reload the city to see it).

options.label: 640 (as shipped)
options.help: The game's own size.
About a third less shadow fill.
Cheapest; softer shadows (at 2x2 resolution, the 3200x2000 size, it is drawn as 768 texels, close to the shipped 640).

settings.label: Sun shadows
settings.help: Full: the game's cascaded sun shadows by day. Fast path: no cascaded shadow maps (about 45 % of the draws), only the fast collector the game uses at night.

options.label: Full (as shipped)
options.help: Cascaded shadow maps.

options.label: Fast path (no cascades)
options.help: No sun shadows by day; the biggest single GPU saving.

settings.label: Shadow distance
settings.help: Scale of the distance within which city sections draw shadows (the game's 200 m). Below 1 saves GPU and CPU. Above 1 = farther than the console (more GPU). Changes at once.

settings.label: City detail distance
settings.help: Scale of the city's high-detail draw distance (the game's 300 m). Below 1 draws fewer far objects. Above 1 = farther than the console (more GPU). Changes at once.

settings.label: Vehicle detail distance
settings.help: Scale of the distances at which vehicles drop to lower LODs. Below 1 lowers them sooner. Above 1 = farther than the console (more GPU). Changes at once.

settings.label: Car reflection update interval
settings.help: 1 = the cars' paint and speedometer reflections are redrawn every frame (the default). 2 = they update at 30 Hz (what the Performance scene-detail preset uses), the frames in between keep the last picture, for a little less GPU load.

settings.label: Reflection view update interval (experimental)
settings.help: The reflection view is redrawn every N-th frame (at 2, on the frames the car-paint reflections are not); the frames in between keep the last picture. Experimental: it uses the same mechanism as the car reflection interval but has not been checked on its own. 1 = every frame (as shipped).

settings.label: Tree impostors
settings.help: Off removes the distant tree impostor sprites (a small saving). Applies to impostors created after the change.

settings.label: Fix grey blocks (no fast clear)
settings.help: Troubleshooting: the game's D3D clear draws one rectangle in the target's own MSAA mode instead of its 4x half-pitch fast clear. Try it if you see grey blocks.

settings.label: Frame rate
settings.help: The game's frame-rate profile. 60 = the full 60 fps timing (quantised simulation, smoothed camera, UI held at 30 Hz, corrected race clock). 30 = locked 30 with the shipped timing. Shipped timing = the game's own present interval, no host cap.

options.label: 60 fps
options.help: The 60 fps profile. Needs a GPU that renders the chosen size in under 16.7 ms; otherwise the game drops to a steady 30 for a while (see Max hold at 30 fps).

options.label: 30 fps (locked)
options.help: The shipped 1/30 s timing, paced to an even 30 fps by the host.

options.label: Shipped timing
options.help: Nothing is set: the guest's own present interval holds 30 fps, no host cap.

settings.label: Late-frame handling
settings.help: At 60 fps the game would hold a frame that arrives a little late for a whole extra refresh (33 ms). Auto releases late frames at once and keeps the real 60 Hz refresh for on-time ones: steadier frame times.

options.label: Auto (recommended)
options.help: Late frames are released immediately while the 60 fps timing is on.

options.label: Off (the game's own)
options.help: A late frame waits for the next refresh.

settings.label: Single-tile scene
settings.help: Draws the 3D scene as one tile instead of two when the whole target fits the emulated EDRAM (4096 tiles, set by the profile). Faster, and required by the FSR upscaler.

settings.label: Max hold at 30 fps (seconds)
settings.help: At 60 fps, when more than about 10 % of frames in a short window miss 60, the game holds 30 fps for a while (a steady 30 beats a 40-50 fps judder), up to this many seconds. 0 = never hold at 30.

settings.label: Frame cap override
settings.help: Overrides the host frame cap that the Frame rate setting chooses. 0 = use the Frame rate setting's own cap. Only 30 and 60 are meaningful.

options.label: From the frame rate setting
options.help: No override.

options.label: 30 fps
options.help: Cap at 30.

options.label: 60 fps
options.help: Cap at 60.

settings.label: CPU boost while playing
settings.help: Changes the active Windows power plan's processor boost setting while the game runs and puts the old value back when the game exits (also after a crash: a small helper restores it, or the next start does). On this laptop the CPU and the GPU share one power budget, so less CPU boost can leave more watts for the GPU. It affects every program while the game runs.

options.label: Leave (Windows decides)
options.help: The power plan is not touched.

options.label: Off while playing
options.help: Processor boost mode is set to Disabled in the active plan (plugged in and on battery) while the game runs.

options.label: Max 99 % while playing
options.help: Maximum processor state is set to 99 % in the active plan (plugged in and on battery) while the game runs; on most AMD systems this also turns boost off. A lower value already set is kept.

settings.label: Asynchronous shader compilation
settings.help: Compiles shaders and pipelines in background threads: less stutter, but a draw may briefly be left out (a flash) while its pipeline is built. Off waits for each shader.

settings.label: Keep the game ahead of other programs
settings.help: Runs the game's frame-critical threads (GPU commands, render, main) at a higher priority on their own fast cores, and shader compiles on the efficient cores. Keeps frames on time while other programs use the CPU; it cannot help when another program uses the GPU.

options.label: On (highest)
options.help: Frame-critical threads at THREAD_PRIORITY_HIGHEST.

options.label: Mild (above normal)
options.help: Frame-critical threads one step above normal.

options.label: Off
options.help: Leave the priorities to Windows.

settings.label: Fence wait instead of spin
settings.help: A GPU fence poll waits briefly for the command processor instead of busy-spinning a CPU core. Off restores the game's own spin loop (more CPU use).

settings.label: Ring-space wait instead of Sleep(0) loop
settings.help: The main thread's wait for space in the command ring sleeps until a slot is released instead of looping on Sleep(0). Same decisions, less CPU. Off restores the game's own loop.

settings.label: Skip the legal screens
settings.help: Skips drawing the legal and logo screens during the boot load. Off plays the game's own boot.

settings.label: Player name
settings.help: The profile name the game shows (the gamertag): 1 to 15 ASCII letters, digits and spaces. Anything else is ignored and the name is 'User'. Read at start.

settings.label: Language
settings.help: The console language the game starts with; it has text for these five languages (any other id gives English). Read at start.

options.label: English
options.help: The default.

options.label: French
options.help: French text (Xbox 360 language id 4).

options.label: German
options.help: German text (id 3).

options.label: Italian
options.help: Italian text (id 6).

options.label: Spanish
options.help: Spanish text (id 5).

settings.label: Pedestrian and parked-car density
settings.help: Scale of pedestrian density and the parked-car fraction in ambient zones. Below 1 = emptier streets and less CPU load. Applies to zones built after the change (the next load).

settings.label: Frame-rate independent camera
settings.help: At 60 fps the chase camera and the chassis ground-depth smoothing keep the 30 fps feel (k(dt) smoothing) instead of the game's own constants. Off gives the raw constants.

settings.label: Race clock
settings.help: How the race clock counts at 60 fps. Retail matches the console (0.99 of real time, 33 ms per 1/30 s); exact is real time; off is the game's own integer maths, about 4 % slow at 60 fps.

options.label: Retail (console-accurate)
options.help: 0.99 of real time with the fraction carried, as on the console.

options.label: Exact
options.help: Real time.

options.label: Off (the game's own)
options.help: The game's int(dt x 1000): about 4 % slow at 60 fps.

settings.label: Menus and HUD at console speed
settings.help: At 60 fps the Flash menus and HUD step 30 times a second, as on the console, and the countdown follows. Off steps them every frame, which runs them at double speed.

settings.label: Menu button repeat fix
settings.help: At 60 fps a held menu button repeats after the console's time (233 ms, then every 200 ms), not after the same number of game updates, which made a tap step a menu twice.

options.label: Auto (on at 60 fps)
options.help: On while the 60 fps timing is on.

options.label: On
options.help: Always use the time-based repeat.

options.label: Off
options.help: The game's own repeat.

settings.label: Title-screen Start fix
settings.help: At 60 fps the title screen and the attract video can miss a press of Start (about half of the presses without this fix). The fix tells the game about a press it missed, once.

options.label: Auto (on at 60 fps)
options.help: On while the 60 fps timing is on.

options.label: On
options.help: Always latch a missed press.

options.label: Off
options.help: The game's own handling.

settings.label: Menu repeat delay (ms)
settings.help: How long a menu button is held before it repeats (the console's 7 updates at 30 a second = 233 ms).

settings.label: Menu repeat interval (ms)
settings.help: The time between repeats of a held menu button (the console's 6 updates at 30 a second = 200 ms).

settings.label: Controller backend
settings.help: How gamepads are read. SDL handles Xbox / generic XInput pads, DualShock 4 and DualSense; XInput reads Windows XInput pads only.

options.label: SDL (all supported pads)
options.help: Xbox, generic XInput, DualShock 4 and DualSense.

options.label: XInput
options.help: Windows XInput controllers only.

settings.label: Keyboard and mouse
settings.help: Emulates a controller from the keyboard (and optionally the mouse), so you can play without a pad. Bindings are under the keyboard rows below.

settings.label: Mouse looks around (right stick)
settings.help: Uses the mouse for the right stick. Off means the right stick comes from the arrow-key bindings only.

settings.label: Mouse sensitivity
settings.help: Mouse sensitivity for the right stick.

settings.label: Keyboard: A button
settings.help: Key(s) for the pad's a button. Comma-separated alternatives ("Q,I"); a Shift+ prefix needs Shift held ("Shift+Up"). Names: A-Z, 0-9, F1-F24, Space, Return, Tab, Backspace, Escape, Up/Down/Left/Right, Semicolon, Quote, Comma, Period, Slash, LBracket, RBracket, Numpad0-9, LMB/RMB/MMB.

settings.label: Keyboard: B button
settings.help: Key(s) for the pad's b button. Comma-separated alternatives ("Q,I"); a Shift+ prefix needs Shift held ("Shift+Up"). Names: A-Z, 0-9, F1-F24, Space, Return, Tab, Backspace, Escape, Up/Down/Left/Right, Semicolon, Quote, Comma, Period, Slash, LBracket, RBracket, Numpad0-9, LMB/RMB/MMB.

settings.label: Keyboard: X button
settings.help: Key(s) for the pad's x button. Comma-separated alternatives ("Q,I"); a Shift+ prefix needs Shift held ("Shift+Up"). Names: A-Z, 0-9, F1-F24, Space, Return, Tab, Backspace, Escape, Up/Down/Left/Right, Semicolon, Quote, Comma, Period, Slash, LBracket, RBracket, Numpad0-9, LMB/RMB/MMB.

settings.label: Keyboard: Y button
settings.help: Key(s) for the pad's y button. Comma-separated alternatives ("Q,I"); a Shift+ prefix needs Shift held ("Shift+Up"). Names: A-Z, 0-9, F1-F24, Space, Return, Tab, Backspace, Escape, Up/Down/Left/Right, Semicolon, Quote, Comma, Period, Slash, LBracket, RBracket, Numpad0-9, LMB/RMB/MMB.

settings.label: Keyboard: Left trigger
settings.help: Key(s) for the pad's left trigger. Comma-separated alternatives ("Q,I"); a Shift+ prefix needs Shift held ("Shift+Up"). settings.label: Mute audio
settings.help: Silences all game audio output.

settings.label: Audio buffer (frames)
settings.help: Maximum buffered audio frames (4-64, 5.3 ms each). Lower reduces latency but may crackle; raise it if the audio stutters.

settings.label: Adaptive audio buffer
settings.help: When the audio output runs dry (the mixer was late), the buffer grows a little from then on so a long stall does not become silence. Costs that much more latency. Restart to apply.

settings.label: Game data folder
settings.help: The folder with the extracted game files: default.xex (9,252,864 bytes) and the four xarchive_*.rpf files. Required: the game cannot start without it.

settings.label: User data folder
settings.help: Where saves, the profile and settings go. Empty = the game's own default (Documents/mcla_x86).

settings.label: Shader cache folder
settings.help: Where the compiled-shader storage is kept. Empty = inside the user data folder. Share one folder between runs to keep the shader cache.

settings.label: Graphics API
settings.help: Which graphics API the game's GPU emulation uses. Direct3D 12 is the tested default (and the only one with the FSR upscaler); Vulkan is available for comparison. Takes effect at start.

options.label: Direct3D 12
options.help: The default; measured about 20 % faster than Vulkan at 720p on a Radeon 880M.

options.label: Vulkan
options.help: For A/B comparison; the FSR upscaler is not available.

settings.label: GPU adapter (Direct3D 12)
settings.help: Index of the DXGI adapter to use: -1 = any physical GPU (a laptop's high-performance GPU is preferred), -2 = software (WARP), 0, 1, ... = that adapter. The game's log lists the adapters.

settings.label: GPU device (Vulkan)
settings.help: Vulkan device index, -1 = automatic selection.

settings.label: Vertical sync (keep on)
settings.help: WARNING: turning this off makes the game's vblank free-run at about 1 kHz, so the game runs far too fast. The 60 fps timing paces itself; leave this on.

settings.label: Log level
settings.help: How much the game writes to its log. Info is normal; trace and debug are very verbose.

options.label: Trace
options.help: Everything; very large logs.

options.label: Debug
options.help: Debug detail.

options.label: Info
options.help: Normal.

options.label: Warnings
options.help: Warnings and errors.

options.label: Errors
options.help: Errors only.

options.label: Critical
options.help: Fatal errors only.

options.label: Off
options.help: No log.

settings.label: Hang watchdog
settings.help: Dumps every guest thread to the log when nothing moves any more. It also writes the heartbeat line that scripted test runs read; harmless to leave on.

settings.label: Optimization: dual-write resolve
settings.help: Direct3D 12: a resolve also writes the host texture directly, so the texture cache does not load it back from shared memory. Exact in the check (15,691 resolved textures, 0 differing); about 0.6 ms less GPU time at 1080p. Turn off to compare or if textures look wrong.

settings.label: Optimization: direct present
settings.help: Direct3D 12: the finished frame goes to the swap chain straight from its render target instead of through an extra full-screen copy. Exact in 155 swap checks; about 0.35 ms less GPU time at 1080p.

settings.label: Optimization: quad lists as triangles
settings.help: Converts the game's quad lists to triangle lists up front: the same triangles on a cheaper path (the picture was identical in the check).

settings.label: Optimization: clear memory page state (off = faster)
settings.help: Off (the default here) keeps uploaded vertex and index memory valid between frames. On is the SDK's old behaviour: it drops every page the GPU did not write at the end of each frame, so 25-30 MB are re-uploaded each frame (about 0.45 CPU core, 0.7 ms GPU). Turn on only if geometry or textures look stale.

settings.label: Optimization: fast-math pixel shaders
settings.help: Direct3D 12: pixel shaders compile in the driver's fast-math mode (fused multiply-add, reassociation): about 20-30 % fewer vector ALU instructions. Last-ulp colour differences only.

settings.label: Optimization: multiply-add in pixel shaders
settings.help: With fast-math pixel shaders: a Xenos mad becomes one multiply-add. The 0 x anything = 0 check is dropped for those terms, so 0 x infinity is NaN there.

settings.label: Optimization: texture sample with LOD bias
settings.help: Direct3D 12: where the hardware computes the texture LOD, pixel shaders sample with sample_b instead of sample_d with scaled derivatives: the same LOD with fewer instructions.

settings.label: Optimization: forward-jump shaders without a loop
settings.help: Direct3D 12: pixel shaders whose control flow is only forward jumps are translated without the main loop used for jumping back, so the compiler need not keep a loop back-edge.

settings.label: Optimization: straight-line vertex fetch
settings.help: Direct3D 12: the vertex fetch is straight-line code (static shared-memory binding, branch-free endian swap), so the driver issues a vertex shader's loads together. The same values.

settings.label: Optimization: skip tone-map transfer (experimental)
settings.help: Experimental, off in the profile: skips the full-screen copy of the scene colour into the tone map's render target where the tone map is proven to rewrite the whole screen. Needs the render markers (switched on automatically). Check the picture.

settings.label: Close the launcher when the game starts
settings.help: Launcher only (not a game option). Off keeps the launcher open and shows "Running..." while the game runs.
